title: How long to plough the field with oxen or a tractor?
description: A tractor ploughs four times faster than a pair of oxen, and the oxen take six hours for one acre. The video finds the time for a twenty acre field with the oxen, then with the tractor, where more speed means less time.
teaching_notes: One idea: more land needs more time in proportion, but a faster machine needs less time, so the time for one acre is divided by the speed factor. Watch for students who multiply six by four and say the tractor takes more time.

video_script.why: The area and the time are in proportion for one machine, but a faster machine takes less time, so the time for an acre is divided by the speed factor.
video_script.substitution: Multiply the acres by the time for one acre for the oxen, and divide the time for one acre by four before multiplying for the tractor.
video_script.anchor: a pair of oxen and a tractor ploughing a field of twenty acres, from the book
video_script.payoff_line: The oxen take one hundred twenty hours, and the tractor takes thirty hours

final_answer.value: 120 hours with oxen and 30 hours with a tractor
final_answer.spoken: one hundred twenty hours with oxen and thirty hours with a tractor

video_script.fraction_reading: one and a half, a quarter
never_show: 6 × 4 = 24 hours for one acre with the tractor, marked as right
maths_rules: oxen: 20 acres × 6 hours for one acre = 120 hours
tractor is 4 times faster, so one acre takes 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 hours
video_script.design: One idea: more land takes more time in proportion, but a faster machine takes less time for each acre. The field and the two machines stay on the stage and the working sits on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about ploughing a field.
<bookmark mark='fast'/>A tractor can plough the same area four times faster than a pair of oxen.
<bookmark mark='oxen'/>A pair of oxen takes six hours to plough one acre of land.
<bookmark mark='field'/>The farmer wants to plough a field of twenty acres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How long will oxen take for the whole field, and how long will a tractor take?

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the time for the whole field with oxen and with the tractor.
<bookmark mark='oxen'/>Step one, start with the oxen. The area and the time are in proportion, so twenty times six gives one hundred twenty.

marks.acre: 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 hours is written under the tractor

narration: <bookmark mark='acre'/>Step two, the tractor is four times faster, so it takes less time for one acre. Six divided by four is one and a half hours.
<bookmark mark='field'/>Step three, the tractor needs twenty times one and a half for the field. That gives thirty.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check. One hundred twenty divided by four is thirty, so the tractor takes a quarter of the oxen time.
